# Long-Period Grating

`maiman.components.LongPeriodGrating` · category **Passive** · [all components](index.md)

Couples the core mode to cladding modes, and transmits what is left.

**What it models.** Coupled-mode theory between the core's LP01 and the first
`cladding_modes` cladding modes of the same azimuthal order -- the only
ones an untilted grating written evenly across the core can reach. The
coupled equations for a uniform grating have constant coefficients, so they
are solved exactly, all modes at once, by diagonalising a small matrix at
every frequency. A notch's depth is `cos^2(kappa L)` at its centre, and its
width is set by how fast the two indices part with wavelength.

**What it does not.** By default the fields are scalar LP modes, and the
cladding-air step is not weak: set `vector` and the block solves the true
HE and EH modes of `maiman.vector_modes` instead, which moves the LP04
notch of the default grating from 1584.1 nm to 1583.0 and adds the weak EH1m
notches the scalar model has no modes for. It costs a few seconds. By
default the indices are constants and only the waveguide disperses; set
`material_dispersion` and the glass does too (silica cladding, germania-doped
core, the quoted indices holding at 1550 nm), which moves the notches by
nanometres, the first cladding mode's 4.2 nm shortward.

**The average index the writing raises.** Compensated by default. Clear
`dc_compensated` and the pedestal `index_modulation / fringe_visibility`
lifts each mode by its own share of it, which moves every notch long by tens
of nanometres -- 20 nm at 1e-4 -- the reason a long-period grating's
resonance is chased during exposure. `resonances` then reports them on
the fibre with its core raised by the pedestal, which the notches agree with
to half a percent.

**Two of them.** A single grating's cladding light is taken to be lost, as it
is under a coating. Set `pair` and the grating is written twice,
`separation` apart over bare fibre, and the second recouples what the first
handed to the cladding: a Mach-Zehnder inside one fibre, its notch filled
with fringes `lambda^2 / (dn_g d)` apart. `gap_loss` is what the cladding
modes lose on the way, which washes the fringes out.

## Ports

| Port | Direction | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `in` | input | optical |
| `transmitted` | output | optical |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `period` | `500.0` | um | 50.0 … 2000.0 | Grating period |
| `length` | `25.0` | mm | 0.1 … 500.0 | Written length |
| `index_modulation` | `0.0003` |  | 0.0 … 0.01 | Index modulation of the core, as for a Bragg grating |
| `dc_compensated` | `True` | flag |  | The writing held the average index flat |
| `fringe_visibility` | `1.0` |  | 0.01 … 1.0 | Fringe amplitude over the average index it sits on (only when `!dc_compensated` is on) |
| `core_radius` | `4.1` | um | 0.5 … 50.0 | Core radius |
| `cladding_radius` | `62.5` | um | 5.0 … 500.0 | Cladding radius |
| `core_index` | `1.4492` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | Core refractive index |
| `cladding_index` | `1.444` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | Cladding refractive index |
| `surrounding_index` | `1.0` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | What the fibre sits in: 1 is air, 1.333 water. Moves every notch |
| `cladding_modes` | `8.0` |  | 1.0 … 40.0 | Cladding modes coupled, highest index first |
| `vector` | `False` | flag |  | Solve the true HE and EH modes instead of the scalar LP ones. Slower |
| `pair` | `False` | flag |  | Write it twice, the cladding bare between: a Mach-Zehnder inside the fibre |
| `separation` | `50.0` | mm | 0.0 … 1000.0 | From the end of one grating to the start of the next (only when `pair` is on) |
| `gap_loss` | `0.0` | dB | 0.0 … 60.0 | Power the cladding modes lose between the two (only when `pair` is on) |
| `material_dispersion` | `False` | flag |  | Let the glass disperse: silica cladding, germania-doped core, the indices above holding at 1550 nm |
